title: ModelRoute
description: A model route the daemon declares: a name, the gateway it goes through ([gateways.<name>] of runbook.toml; a lone [gateway] table is the gateway `default`), the gateway's alias of the model and its kind (a daemon that declares no route but has a lone [gateway] table and a model decider declares the interim route `default` on that gateway: kind hosted, its alias the model of the decider, no price), with what the daemon last read of the gateway: the wires `GET /v1/models` lists for the alias and the route's status. The daemon reads its file when it starts and the gateway when a client asks for the view Routes, at most once every 15 seconds (the rows of a read are kept and answered until then); the language cannot read a file or a gateway, so no command creates or changes a row, as with Runbook. No address, token, token file or price is in a row.

gateway.description: The name of the route's gateway in the daemon's file, never its address.

alias.description: The model's alias at the gateway: what the gateway's `GET /v1/models` lists and a model call names.

wires.description: The wires the gateway lists for the alias (chat, responses, messages), in its order; none when the gateway did not answer or does not list the alias.

phase.description: The phase the gateway gave for the route's model (ready, starting, stopped, stopping, unreachable, or a phase the gateway adds later); absent when no status of the model was read.

max_model_len.description: The context length `GET /v1/models` gave for the alias; absent when the gateway gave none.

tool_calling.description: Whether the model calls tools, as `GET /v1/models` gave it for the alias (a boolean `tool_calling`); absent when the gateway gave nothing.

start_wait_seconds.description: The route's start_wait_seconds of the daemon's file: how long a run waits for the route's model to be ready (WaitForRoute), and how long after a wake of the route a run joins it (wake_joinable). Present when the file declares it, for a route of any kind; absent otherwise.

wake_booked_micro_usd.description: What the route's wakes booked on the day of the daemon's clock (UTC): those the gateway took (a 2xx answer) and those still out, the figure the cap of the next wake reads (WaitForRoute). Present for a managed route that declares wake_daily_cap_micro_usd, else absent.

wake_cap_micro_usd.description: The route's wake_daily_cap_micro_usd: what its wakes and its pod's time may book per day. Absent when the route is not managed or declares none.

wake_cost_micro_usd.description: The route's wake_cost_micro_usd: what one wake books. Present with wake_cap_micro_usd when the file declares it.

wake_last_sent_at.description: The instant of the newest run event `runbook.route-wake` of the route that was sent, on any day, whatever its answer. Present with wake_cap_micro_usd once a wake of the route was sent.

wake_last_answer.description: How the wake that wake_last_sent_at names was answered, one word per case: `2xx`, `4xx`, `5xx` (the class of the gateway's status; `1xx` and `3xx` alike), `spend-ceiling` (the gateway's code `spend-ceiling`, whatever the status), `no-answer` (no answer within the daemon's bound of 5 s: the status is null), `none-yet` (not answered yet while the wake is in flight: its run lives, or its run was closed and this daemon still waits for the answer) or `lost` (never answered: the daemon went away while it was out). Read from the run event `runbook.route-wake-answered`, or the daemon's journal line `route.wake-answered` of a run closed before it came. The newest wake's answer, not the instant of a send, is what ends a ceiling for a client: ceiling_refused_at keeps its meaning. Present with wake_last_sent_at.

wake_last_answered_at.description: The instant of that answer: the `at` of its run event `runbook.route-wake-answered` or of the daemon's line `route.wake-answered`. Present with wake_last_answer, except for `none-yet` and `lost`.

wake_needed.description: True when the route's wake is on (wake_on_submit), the phase of this row is `stopped`, a run that takes the route (or a delegation the daemon classifies, on the classifier route) is WaitingForRoute, no wake of the route is out (sent, not answered yet, its run live, also past the wait) and none may be joined (one within the route's start_wait_seconds that the gateway took or answered `spend-ceiling`, or that is out, failed or not answered while its run lives): a run waits and the daemon sends no wake for it, because the wake would pass the day's cap, was answered 4xx, or the wake the run joined is past its wait. False otherwise. Present with wake_cap_micro_usd.

wake_joinable.description: True when the route's wake is on (wake_on_submit) and a run submitted now that wakes the route would join a wake in flight and send and book none, by the rule the wake itself applies: the newest sent wake of the route less than the route's start_wait_seconds old that may still start the model (answered 2xx or `spend-ceiling`, or answered 5xx, not answered in time or not answered yet while its run lives). False otherwise, also with the wake off. It does not say whether a run submitted now wakes the route at all: that turns on the phase of this row being `stopped`. wake_needed says something else: a run waits now and no wake is sent for it. Present with wake_cap_micro_usd.

wake_joinable_sent_at.description: The instant of the wake a run would join: the `at` of its run event `runbook.route-wake`, the `joined_at` a joining run records. Present while wake_joinable is true.

wake_joinable_until.description: wake_joinable_sent_at plus the route's start_wait_seconds: a run submitted before this instant joins the wake; it may stop being joinable sooner (a 4xx answer, its run ending without a 2xx). Present while wake_joinable is true.

ceiling_refused_at.description: The instant of the newest answer `spend-ceiling` to a wake of the route on the day of the daemon's clock: a run event `runbook.route-wake-answered`, or the daemon's journal line `route.wake-answered` of a run closed before it came. Absent when there is none that day.

wake_cap_refused_at.description: The instant of the newest run event `runbook.route-wake` of the route on the day of the daemon's clock that was not sent for the wake cap (reason `wake cap reached`). Absent when there is none that day; a later wake of the day that was sent leaves it.

wake_cap_refused_cap_micro_usd.description: The `cap_micro_usd` of that refusal: the wake cap in force when it was refused. A client compares it with wake_cap_micro_usd, the cap declared now (the daemon reads the cap at its start): a refusal under a cap since raised no longer holds. Present with wake_cap_refused_at.

pod_booked_micro_usd.description: What the pod's time of the route booked on the day of the daemon's clock up to now at its price_per_hour_micro_usd, each run's share, also of runs that still live: the other part of what the cap counts. A wake is not sent when wake_booked_micro_usd plus this plus wake_cost_micro_usd is above wake_cap_micro_usd. Present for a managed route that declares price_per_hour_micro_usd, else absent.

daily_booked_micro_usd.description: What the relay booked on the route on the day of the daemon's clock (UTC): the sum of the ledger lines of the calls sent on that day, each at its cost, or at its reservation when its cost is not known; a call counts when its answer has ended. The figure daily_cap_micro_usd is held against: a call is sent while this is below the cap. Present for every route.

daily_cap_micro_usd.description: The route's daily_cap_micro_usd: the most the relay may book on it per day, on a route of any kind that declares a price. Absent when the route declares none.

daily_llm_calls.description: The calls the relay sent on the route on the day of the daemon's clock (UTC), each counted as it was admitted. Present for every route.

daily_max_llm_calls.description: The route's daily_max_llm_calls: the most calls the relay may send on it per day. Absent when the route declares none.

read_at.description: When the daemon read the gateway for this row.

sdc.daemon.ModelRouteKind.title: ModelRouteKind
sdc.daemon.ModelRouteKind.description: What stands behind a route's alias at its gateway: managed (a model on a pod the gateway starts and stops), hosted (a fixed upstream, nothing started) or local (a model server on the gateway's machine, such as Ollama). The daemon's file says which; the daemon reads the status of a managed or a local route from the gateway, and sends a hosted route no call to probe it.

sdc.daemon.RouteName.title: RouteName
sdc.daemon.RouteName.description: The name of a model route the daemon declares (a table [routes.<name>] of its runbook.toml): one to 64 characters of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`. A client names a route by it, never by an address, a token or an alias; the address, the token file and the prices stay in the daemon's file.

sdc.daemon.RouteStatus.title: RouteStatus
sdc.daemon.RouteStatus.description: Where a route stands as the daemon last read its gateway: gateway-unreachable (no answer from `GET /ready` or `GET /v1/models`, or an address the daemon does not speak, https), gateway-not-ready (`/ready` answered, not 200, or `/v1/models` gave no list), model-unknown (the gateway is ready and `GET /v1/models` does not list the route's alias), ready or not-ready (the gateway read the route's model: `callable` of `GET /v1/status`, else the phase of `GET /v1/models/{alias}/status` for a managed or a local route, ready only for the phase ready), listed (the gateway is ready and lists the alias, and no status of the model was read: a hosted route on a gateway without `/v1/status`, or a status route that did not answer). A read sends no model call and starts nothing.
